utterances.text: May I just add a coda to that, with respect, and it's intended to be as much for Mr. Antic's, if you like, protection and support as anything. It is extremely awkward sometimes, we've found, for witness who are in The Hague. They often find themselves in very close proximity to other witnesses in the same case. Your Honour will appreciate, of course, Mr. Antic, the technical position, of course, is that they are free human beings and two witnesses in the same case can talk to each other about football or whatever they wish, but we would very respectfully suggest that, as far as possible, Mr. Antic might feel that it was better to avoid being drawn into social contact with other witnesses in this case, just for his own protection and to ensure that nobody's tempted to cross over that line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, I don't know whether you followed it, but when I instructed you not to speak with anyone else about your testimony, Mr. Stewart has drawn my attention to the fact that you might see other persons which might be interested to discuss with you your testimony. Perhaps even if you want to talk about football, perhaps you'd delay that until the next football match and refrain from it this evening and tomorrow morning. We all expect your testimony to finish tomorrow. So to refrain from social contacts of those with whom you might be very well able to speak about football, but also about other subjects. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. I don't wish to protract today's session, but I have a quick scheduling clarification which I seek, and that is, anticipating that we'll conclude this witness's testimony tomorrow, will we be starting with the next witness tomorrow? That was not entirely clear to me, based on the information we received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart. You were asked last time not to immediately follow the next witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. May I leave it this way, Your Honour: We're tomorrow afternoon, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: If we were sitting tomorrow afternoon, the answer would, I'm afraid, be it's incredibly difficult. May I explore that in the course of this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the Prosecution would like to know for their scheduling and for preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, if they want to know, then the answer -- I'm trying to be helpful, Your Honour. If they want to know now, then the answer will be, no, we won't be able to follow. What I was intending to explore in the afternoon was whether, given the way the timetable is shaping up, whether we could in fact bring that witness forward to start immediately tomorrow if that were helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no preference, but you just want to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: If it doesn't matter to Mr. Tieger or the Prosecution or indeed to the Trial Chamber if we say we would like to start that witness on Wednesday morning, then the Defence will be happy to have that simply clear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least if you're not getting into trouble by the end of the week, we'll leave it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We don't anticipate a difficulty about that, Your Honour, at the other end of the week.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as you noted, I was simply seeking enhanced understanding of the situation, not taking a position on it. Insofar as I'm aware, that's not a problem, but I needed to hear what the situation was before we could figure out what our response was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm just really trying to be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We now expect the Defence to start the examination of the next witness on Wednesday afternoon, and if they want to avoid all risks, they should inform the -- and if they want to start on Tuesday in the afternoon, immediately following this witness, then they should inform the Prosecution within one hour from now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's very helpful, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So I said already that we adjourn. Courtroom II tomorrow, a quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 8th day of November 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.54 p.m.,
